title: Psychodynamic therapy and cognitive-behavioral therapy for obsessive-compulsive disorder: a randomized-controlled study
summary: The purpose of the study is to compare two different treatment methods for people with obsessive-compulsive disorder: psychodynamic therapy (PDT) and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT). Patients are randomly assigned to treatment conditions. First, all patients receive 24 sessions of exposure with response management (ERM), i.e., therapy in which patients learn to face situations they fear or avoid consciously and to allow the feelings associated with them without performing their compulsive acts. In one condition it is carried out by therapists trained in cognitive-behavioral therapy, in the other condition by therapists trained in psychodynamic therapy. In these 24 sessions, both follow the same manual, in the latter variant (PDT) exposure with response man-agement based on a psychodynamic therapy conceptualization and stance is performed (Freud, 1919 S.191-192, Leichsenring & Steinert, 2017, 2019).  Subsequently, depending on the assigned group, patients will re-ceive either 1) further CBT of 36 sessions, in which patients will practice specific skills (continuation of exposure or other skills in dealing with other OCD-related issues such as social skills, building enjoyable activities) or a 2) psychodynamic therapy of another 36 sessions that works with the central relationship conflict theme (ZBKT) underlying the obsessive-compulsive symptoms and follows the Manual for the Treatment of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorders by Leichsenring and Steinert (2017; 2019). Experiences from exposure will be related to the ZBKT and used to modify it. The effectiveness of both options will be compared using standardized meas-urement instruments.

interventions.name: CBT-ERM (cognitive-behavioral therapy-exposure with response management) & CBT

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Presence of a diagnosed obsessive-compulsive disorder (ICD-10: F42 or obsessive-compulsive disorder according to DSM-5 as the primary diagnosis. The diagnosis is made by means of a SKID interview according to DSM-5.
- Willingness and consent to participate in the study including randomization (informed consent); ability to give consent
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
- Willingness and indication for long-term psychotherapeutic treatment of OCD (long-term psychotherapy, 60 sessions)
Exclusion criteria:
- Hoarding disorder
- Psychotic disorders according to ICD-10 chapter F2, bipolar disorders (ICD-10 F31 or F34.0)
- There must be an indication for primary treatment of the obsessive-compulsive disorder. However, comorbid F-diagnoses do not constitute an exclusion criterion as long as the treatment of the comorbid disease is not a priority.
